title: Lynn Well Depth and Drilling Cost
meta_description: Lynn wells have a 222-foot median depth, 6.0 gpm median yield, and estimated finished costs of $13,800-$24,200.
h1: Lynn, Colorado Well Depth, Yield, and Cost
intro_html:
Buying land near Lynn means looking past the presence of a well permit. The local record shows 234 permitted wells within 5 miles, but only 161 report total depth, 53 report pump yield, and 17 report static water level. That makes the available numbers useful for planning, not a guarantee for a particular lot.

Lynn is on the plains, where wells are recorded in unnamed or fractured-bedrock aquifers rather than the Denver Basin. Nearby context includes Aguilar, about 1 mile away, and El Moro and Walsenburg, both about 16 miles away. Check the actual permit, construction report, and neighboring wells before you commit to a property.

sections.heading: Lynn well depths vary sharply across the plains
sections.html:
The median reported well depth near Lynn is 222 feet. The middle half runs from 57 to 563 feet, so a driller bidding a new well has a wide local range to consider. One well reaches 2,458 feet, and 24% of reported wells are 600 feet or deeper.

The depth mix is spread out: 34% are under 100 feet, 21% fall between 100 and 300 feet, 22% between 300 and 600 feet, and 24% are 600 feet or deeper. That spread points to changing sediment and bedrock conditions from lot to lot. Use the median as a starting point for a bid, not as a promised target depth. Ground conditions, casing, grout, access, and the result of drilling all affect the final job.

sections.heading: Most Lynn wells make usable household quantities
sections.html:
Among the 53 wells with a reported pump yield, the median is 6.0 gallons per minute. The middle half produces 4.0 to 9.0 gallons per minute. That is a reasonable planning range for a household well, but the yield record is incomplete and a nearby result does not prove the same result on your lot.

Only 2% of reported wells are under 1 gallon per minute. Another 30% produce 1 to 5 gallons per minute, 58% produce 5 to 15 gallons per minute, and 9% produce more than 15 gallons per minute. Ask for the well completion report and pump test, then have a contractor size the pump, pressure tank, and storage around the actual result. Fractured-bedrock wells can be unpredictable over short distances.

sections.heading: Lynn water levels are recorded, but not as a trend
sections.html:
The 17 wells reporting static water level have a median depth to water of 57 feet. The middle half runs from 35 to 235 feet below ground. These figures help with pump planning, trenching, and estimating how much lift the system may need, but they are not a water-table measurement for every parcel.

The permit totals by decade show activity rather than groundwater decline: 2 permits in the 1960s, 12 in the 1970s, 5 in the 1980s, 49 in the 1990s, 77 in the 2000s, 30 in the 2010s, and 17 in the 2020s. Because static levels are reported for only 17 wells and no comparable decade series is provided, this record does not establish a dropping water table. Request a current water-level check when buying.

sections.heading: Lynn drilling history includes recent permits
sections.html:
The records include permits from the 1960s through the 2020s, with the newest permit year listed as 2025. The use mix is primarily domestic or household at 65%, with stock use at 37%. Irrigation accounts for 5%, and monitoring accounts for 12%; some permits can have more than one use designation.

The most active drillers in these records are Boday Well Drilling, listed with Kathleen Boday, with 26 wells; Weber Water Well Drilling & Pump Service LLC, listed with David J. Weber, with 21; and Sharpe Drilling Co, listed with Lyle M. Sharpe, with 18. These names describe permit history, not a recommendation. Confirm current licensing, availability, scope, and warranty before hiring. A Colorado DWR permit and the construction report are important parts of the property file.

sections.heading: What a new Lynn well may cost
sections.html:
For Lynn's alluvium and plains sedimentary rock, the drilling model uses $35 to $55 per foot. At the 222-foot median depth, the drilled hole works out to about $7,800 to $12,200. That is only the hole. A finished system with pump, pressure tank, trenching, and electrical is estimated at about $13,800 to $24,200 at the same depth.

Depth is the main reason the estimate can move. A well in the 600-foot-plus group will not fit the median-depth budget, and a 2,458-foot record shows that very deep outcomes exist locally. Get a written bid that separates drilling, casing, grout, development, pump equipment, electrical, trenching, access, and unsuccessful-hole terms. Ask what happens if the well is deeper than the initial allowance.

sections.heading: Checks before building or buying near Lynn
sections.html:
Low yield is not the only risk. Review the 15 PFAS sampling or contamination sites mapped within about 10 miles and ask for a certified water test for the property well. The area also has 187 historic mine features. There are 0 EPA Superfund or cleanup sites mapped, but that does not replace a site-specific inspection or laboratory testing.

Confirm the well's casing, grout, pump setting, static level, and construction report. Septic placement and repair access need to protect the well from contamination and leave room for service equipment. Before building, confirm the DWR permit allows the intended household or stock use. In an over-appropriated basin, additional water use may require an augmentation plan. Have the septic designer, excavator, and well contractor review the lot together.

faq.q: How deep are wells in Lynn, Colorado?
faq.a: The median reported well depth within 5 miles of Lynn is 222 feet. The middle half ranges from 57 to 563 feet. Local results are widely spread: 34% are under 100 feet, while 24% are 600 feet or deeper. One recorded well reaches 2,458 feet, so a nearby well is useful for planning but cannot guarantee your depth.

faq.q: How much does it cost to drill a well in Lynn?
faq.a: The local drilling model uses $35 to $55 per foot. At the 222-foot median depth, the drilled hole is estimated at $7,800 to $12,200. A finished well with pump, tank, trenching, and electrical is estimated at $13,800 to $24,200. Deeper drilling, difficult access, casing, and site-specific electrical or trenching needs can change the bid.

faq.q: How much water does a well produce in Lynn?
faq.a: The median reported pump yield is 6.0 gallons per minute, with the middle half from 4.0 to 9.0 gallons per minute. Among reported yields, 2% are under 1 gallon per minute, 30% are 1 to 5, and 58% are 5 to 15. Only 53 wells report yield, so require a pump test for the property.

faq.q: Is well water safe in Lynn, Colorado?
faq.a: Do not assume a private well is safe because it has a permit. The mapped area includes 15 PFAS sampling or contamination sites and 187 historic mine features within about 10 miles. Have the property water tested by a certified laboratory, review the well construction report, and ask about nearby land uses. No EPA Superfund or cleanup sites are mapped.

faq.q: Are there recent well permits near Lynn?
faq.a: Yes. The records include permits through 2025. Permit activity includes 77 permits in the 2000s, 30 in the 2010s, and 17 in the 2020s. The most active names in the records are Boday Well Drilling with 26 wells, Weber Water Well Drilling & Pump Service LLC with 21, and Sharpe Drilling Co with 18.
